newsitem.title: ITALY: SOCCER SHOWCASE-FACTS AND FIGURES FOR MILAN V SAMPDORIA.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER SHOWCASE-FACTS AND FIGURES FOR MILAN V SAMPDORIA.

text.p: Facts and figures for Sunday's Italian serie A match between Milan and Sampdoria at the San Siro stadium:
Formed 1899 by Englishman Alfred Edwards as Milan Cricket and Football Club, became Milan Associazione Calcio in 1939. They have won the league title 15 times.

Major honours: European champions: 1963, 1969, 1989, 1990, 1994. European Cup Winners' Cup winners 1968, 1973. Intercontinental Cup: 1969, 1989, 1990. European Supercup: 1989, 1990, 1995. Italian champions: 1901, 1906, 1907, 1951, 1955, 1957, 1959, 1962, 1968, 1979, 1988, 1992, 1993, 1994, 1996. Italian Cup winners: 1967, 1972, 1973, 1977.
Ground: Stadio Giuseppe Meazza, San Siro, capacity 85,700

Formed 1946, Sampdoria is one of the youngest clubs in serie A. Product of union between two historic Genovese clubs, Andrea Doria (established 1895) and Sampiedarenese (established 1899). They have won the league title once.
Major honours: European Cup Winners' Cup winners 1990. Italian champions 1991. Italian Cup winners 1985, 1988, 1989, 1994.
First league meeting in Milan: March 9, 1947, Milan 1 Sampdoria 0

Record victories: Milan beat Sampdoria 6-1 on September 25, 1955. In the same season, on March 25, 1956, Samp lost 7-1 to Internazionale Milan at the same San Siro ground - their heaviest serie A defeat ever.
Sampdoria have twice beaten Milan 3-0 in Genoa, including on the penulitimate match of last season, the week after Milan were crowned champions.
Milan v Sampdoria last 10 seasons from 1986-87 (Milan first): 0-2, 2-1, 0-0, 1-0, 0-1, 5-1, 4-0, 1-0, 0-0, 3-0
Corresponding match last season: January 7, 1996, Milan 3 (Panucci 10, Savicevic 37, Baggio 56) Sampdoria 0, attendance 55,000

- Roberto Mancini, with 138 league goals, is the most prolific striker currently playing in Italy but the former international has only scored five career goals against Milan, and just twice at the San Siro.
- Milan's Roberto Baggio is the second most prolific striker in serie A with 130 career goals.

- Sampdoria won their first ever major trophy at Milan's expense in the 1985 Italian Cup final: Samp won the first leg 1-0 in Milan with a goal from Scotland's Graeme Souness, and clinched victory with a 2-1 victory in the return leg in Genoa.
- In the clubs' one clash in Europe, Milan claimed the 1990 European Supercup with a 3-1 aggregate victory.
